newsitem.title: HUNGARY: HUNGARY APV NOT TO DECIDE ON PAYMENTS TO FIRMS.
newsitem.headline: HUNGARY APV NOT TO DECIDE ON PAYMENTS TO FIRMS.

text.p: A decision on planned payments to Hungarian companies from the state privatisation agency APV is not on the agenda of the APV board's weekly meeting on Wednesday, APV spokesman Adam Dudits told Reuters on Monday.
"That's not on the agenda," he said, but added that the agenda may change until Wednesday.
A 1989 law promised state-owned companies which transformed themselved into shareholder companies before 1992 that they would receive 20 percent of all subsequent privatisation revenues.
APV said last week that it would probably transfer some 10 billion to 12 billion forints to part of these firms by June 30, and a similar amount was likely to be paid out later in the summer.

Market speculation that the payments from APV would boost chemicals company TVK's earnings in the first half of the year propelled the price of TVK shares to record highs on the Budapest Stock Exchange (BSE) in the past week.

Analysts said earlier that the payments may affect many of the BSE's leading companies, including oil and gas company MOL, pharmaceuticals Egis , tile maker Zalakeramia , meet processor Pick and OTP Bank .
